Evidence and limitations

This explains general trade-offs. It cannot choose an implant, predict postoperative vision, or determine whether night driving is safe.

Comparison assumption: both Monofocal eyes target distance, with appropriate refractive correction. Monovision, with one eye targeting distance and the other near, is a separate option. We do not deliberately leave astigmatism uncorrected to exaggerate differences.

The images use a simplified Trifocal teaching model: three PSFs each carry one third of the intensity, with focal powers of 0, 1.25 and 2.5 D in one effective optical plane, corresponding to distance, 80 cm and 40 cm. The pupil is 4 mm and wavelength 550 nm. These teaching parameters are not measurements of any IOL and cannot predict halo shape, intensity, adaptation or postoperative vision. Enhanced monofocal and EDOF use symbolic focus-range diagrams only. Daytime photos are treated as distant scenes, without depth-layer calculations. The astigmatism topic assumes 1.00 D of regular astigmatism, comparing ideal glasses with an aligned Toric IOL; the axis slider illustrates rotation from 0–30°. Both sides use the same single-focus optics. At intermediate and near distances, both receive the ideal additional power for the target, isolating the astigmatism comparison.

Source checks and numerical validation are documented in thevalidation record. This app has not been reviewed by an ophthalmologist.

The photos contain their own imaging artifacts and have limited dynamic range. Convolution is calculated in linear light. Main street scenes assume a 40° horizontal field; other scenes use 8°. The generated photos have no measured camera field. The halo / haze slider is an additional visual illustration control: it blends B’s model rendering with an ideally focused reference in linear light. Lower settings reduce added halos and haze. It does not model lens designs, optical efficiency, neuroadaptation or surgical success. Its endpoints and default are not clinically calibrated. One setting carries across night, daytime, reading and arm-length scenes; lower values also make near and intermediate targets appear clearer. Each scene uses an ideally focused reference at its own distance. This is not one physically consistent IOL model: the minimum does not establish a lens that focuses perfectly at every distance without optical trade-offs. Astigmatism illustrations are unaffected. Technical PSF plots remain only in the optional independent laboratory. Near and intermediate scenes initially show no glasses on either side. Putting on glasses ideally adds the power needed by A at the current distance. The 80 cm and 40 cm additions differ; this is not one pair of glasses working equally well at all distances. Neither side in the lens-type comparison has residual astigmatism. Research background for weighted PSF simulation—this app has not undergone the clinical calibration or validation used in that study.
